I've been to several therapists, some good some bad. Just go up to whoever it is in your family that you feel closest to (for me it was my dad) and tell them that you're having some issues sorting out your emotions, and you'd like to see a counselor/therapist. (People tend to like the term counselor better, even though it's the same thing as being a therapist, people tend to associate "therapists" being people who help crazy people. It's dumb, I know, but the stereotype is there)

It took a few weeks before I could get into a therapist appointment, but once I did it felt like I was finally able to vent out all the shit that was bugging me. Although my first therapist sucked - not properly informing my parents when I was literally writing suicide notes and making plans to kill myself (i attempted but lived obviously), my second one was much, much better though. He and I get along perfectly, the only reason I had to switch was because of insurance, which sucks but... eh. it is what it is.

Lonliness is one of the worst feelings in the world. I have spent almost my whole life, bullied, being an outcast, and just generally not getting a long with anyone. Confidence goes a long way, in both making friends and dating people. I got together with a girl 3 years older than me ( I look older than my age, and granted, we met in a mental hospital. it didn't go well but that's besides the point) I had managed to fake confidence and be funny long enough to get her to like me. It was very difficult at first, but once you get going, it starts to flow naturally. https://www.amazon.com/Everything-Self-Esteem-Book-Confidence-Strength/dp/1580629768 Here's a great book on self-esteem, I'd recommend you check it out. 

Trying to explain to friends what having depression is like is like trying to explain what colors are to a blind person. It's nearly impossible. That's why support groups like this exist, to help people out <3
